## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `b220ce83e716c7d47498b48e48ee5e4df2f91c30`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37556 (body, triage, claim, os-dev report), PR #37571 (body, 3-file list, net diff against `main`), and the 55 check-runs on the head (40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed; required aggregates `Test UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` all success). Files outside the diff (`ChatDock.tsx`, `use-mobile.tsx`, `AppContent.tsx`, `AiAddressRedirect.tsx`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `usePhoneNavDrawerHistory.ts`) were read for context only, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: none changed. No schema, validator, parser or permission check is in the diff. Right.
- Public surface: none changed. `useConsoleChatDock` keeps its signature and return shape; the two storage helpers and `DOCK_SHEET_SHOWN_AT_STORAGE_KEY` are module-private. The one new persisted artifact is a per-tab sessionStorage key `ai-chat-dock-sheet-shown-at`, internal to the hook. Right.
- Behaviour surface (intended, and wider than "chat navigations"): on a phone, ANY router PUSH or POP away from the entry the sheet was shown on now collapses the sheet, whatever started it: a citation chip, `open_record`, a list link, the phone Back button, or the nav drawer's own history push. The PR body names this ("every navigation the chat makes"); the code applies it to every navigation, which the card's rule allows. It reaches all three hosts (`ConsoleLayout`, `HomeLayout`, `DesktopDocsPortalShell`), which share the key and swap with each other. Right.
- Fence held: the diff touches none of PR #37539's files, nothing under `packages/**`, `skills/**` or `docs/adr/**`.

Graded findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — A cross-layout PUSH can leave the sheet open when a REPLACE lands during the new host's mount. The real `useIsMobile` returns `false` on a host's first render (`useState(undefined)`, `!!isMobile`), so a freshly mounted host (Home to an app, one app to another) runs the new effect for the first time on its second render. React batches any REPLACE that a child's mount effect issues in that first commit into the same render. Then `navigationType` is `REPLACE` and the sheet is re-stamped as shown on the new key, not collapsed. A concrete path exists: `AppContent` (which renders `ConsoleLayout`) moves an app-name alias URL to the package-id address with `navigate(..., { replace: true })` on mount. So an `open_record` or chip link that names the app by alias, followed from Home, leaves the sheet over the page. The test can't catch this because its `useIsMobile` mock returns the measured value on the first render. Suggested fix: treat the first evaluation in a host (or one where the stored entry is not this host's previous key) as PUSH/POP even under REPLACE when `shownAt` names an entry this host never saw. Alternatively, record the PUSH/POP before the mobile flag settles. Then add a case to the two-layout test where the landing route replaces on mount and the mock returns `false` on the first render.
- S2 (should-fix) — The test has no POP case. The rule the code comment and PR body state is "PUSH or POP", and the seat brief asks for POP, but no case navigates back (for example `navigate(-1)` after opening the sheet on a pushed entry). The branch is shared with PUSH, so the risk is low, but the stated behaviour is not pinned.
- N1 (nit) — The stored entry is never cleared or refreshed while the host is at desktop width (the effect returns early when `!isMobile`). On a tablet that rotates across the 768 px breakpoint, this sequence collapses the sheet on rotation rather than on a navigation: sheet open in portrait, rotate to landscape (the rail shows), PUSH to another page, rotate back. The early return cannot simply clear the key, because the same early return covers a phone host's first render (see S1). It needs the same "measured" signal.
- N2 (nit) — `BrowserRouter` gives the first entry of every document load the key `"default"`. Suppose the sheet was shown on a first entry and the tab then makes a full document load to another URL. The stale `"default"` reads as "shown here" and the sheet stays open, which was the behaviour before the PR, so the effect is benign. Comparing on `pathname+search` plus key would remove the collision.
- N3 (nit) — The jsdoc says "A private-mode storage failure just means a navigation that remounts the layout does not close the sheet." That understates the failure. With storage throwing, `readSheetShownAt()` always returns `null`, so no navigation closes the sheet, including on the same host. The page still works; the fix just goes inert. Either correct the comment or keep an in-memory fallback ref.
- N4 (nit) — The os-dev report says "CI Test UI 16/16 shards success". The head carries nine leg runs (`Test UI (1/16)` to `(9/16)`, an affected plan) under a green `Test UI` aggregate. The aggregate is the gate and it is green; only the report's count is wrong.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/37556-phone-dock-closes-on-citation.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The diff publishes only a behaviour fix inside an existing hook: no export, type or prop added, removed or changed. Patch is right. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.
- Clause-②: no — right. The change touches no published spec, schema, metadata key or governed path. It is UI hook internals plus a test and a changeset, and the PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching the card's acceptance line.
- Metadata-protocol: none — right. No metadata is read, written or declared differently. The only new persisted value is a per-tab sessionStorage key in the browser.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: `open_questions` is `[]`; `out_of_scope_findings` is `none`; `security_findings` is `none`. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- The PR body says "declared narrowing" for leaving the whole `@object-ui/app-shell` suite to CI. That is a test-run scope note, not a `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` arm. No narrowing face applies, and CI `Test UI` is green.
- Acceptance 2 (booted phone screenshot) is described in the PR body with paths in the project files, not in the PR. It was taken on a local merge with PR #37539, and the citations part was injected (disclosed). It was not verified from this seat (read-only); it is noted, not graded.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff makes no data read, materialises no ids and does no in-app join; it is router and sessionStorage state only.

Seat questions:

1. Phone PUSH/POP collapses, REPLACE never, conversation kept, desktop untouched. Mostly yes. The effect returns at once when `!isMobile`, so no desktop path calls `collapse()`. `collapse` is guarded by `navigationType !== NavigationType.Replace`, so no REPLACE collapses. `collapse()` only flips `expanded` and full-window and leaves `target` untouched, so reopening shows the same thread (the test pins this). PUSH and POP away from the stored entry collapse, including a same-URL PUSH (fresh key). The exception, in the not-collapsing direction, is S1: a cross-layout PUSH followed by a mount-time REPLACE stays open. N1 is a collapse on a phone rotation, not on desktop.
2. Stale or foreign key. A foreign tab cannot reach it: sessionStorage is per tab, and a duplicated tab copies storage and `history.state` keys together. A reload is right: `BrowserRouter` keeps `location.key` in `history.state`, so the key matches and the sheet stays as before. A previous sheet's key is cleared on every close the host sees at phone width, so it does not leak, with two exceptions. First, a sheet left open across a desktop-width period (N1) gives a wrong collapse on return to phone width. Second, the `"default"` first-entry key across document loads (N2) wrongly reads as "shown here", which is benign. Storage throwing: both helpers are in try/catch and the page renders and works, but the fix goes fully inert, not "remount only" as the jsdoc says (N3).
3. The test. The three phone-click cases (PUSH, same-URL PUSH, two-layout remount) are real negative controls: they go red with `collapse()` no-op'd (dev ablation: 3 red, 2 green), and the two-layout case also goes red against a hook-local rule. The REPLACE case and the desktop control stay green under that ablation, but by reading they are real controls for their own clauses: dropping the `Replace` exemption turns the REPLACE case red, and dropping the `!isMobile` guard turns the desktop control red. Covered: PUSH, REPLACE, second-layout remount. Not covered: POP (S2), and the real `useIsMobile` first-render `false` on remount (S1).
4. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at patch: right for an internal UI hook behaviour fix with no export, schema or metadata change (see ②).

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are should-fix and may land as a follow-up card in the same area.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `b220ce83e716c7d47498b48e48ee5e4df2f91c30`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: draft against `main`. Three files under `ui/packages/app-shell`, plus a patch changeset. Not governed, not security-touching. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.
2. **Premise**: on a phone, a PUSH or POP away from the entry the sheet was shown on collapses it, and a REPLACE never does. Keeping the shown-at key per tab in sessionStorage, with try/catch around every read and write, is sound.
3. **Gates**: contract record 7195408408 (`TIER_DEFAULT`) reads PASS, with two should-fix findings owed before landing. CI on this head: 0 failed.
4. **Owed before landing** (ids from the record):
   - **S1**: a new layout host's first render reads `useIsMobile` as `false`, so a REPLACE that a child issues on mount (for example `AppContent`'s alias-to-package-id redirect) counts as "stay open". A chip or `open_record` link that names the app by alias, followed from Home, then leaves the sheet over the page. Don't let a REPLACE issued before the phone flag settles cancel a pending collapse. Pin it with a test whose `useIsMobile` mock starts `false` on the first render.
   - **S2**: add a POP (Back) case to the test.
5. **Ride along if cheap** (not blocking): N3 (correct the storage-failure comment), N1 (clear the key at desktop width). N2 and N4 are accepted.
6. **Landing terms**: after the delta the same reviewer re-checks it. Then the area lands it. Post a phone screenshot of the alias path on the delta.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e4692c39299349d37127805653a7925d7962539a`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review. The previous record covered head `b220ce83e716c7d47498b48e48ee5e4df2f91c30` and read PASS with S1 and S2 owed. The seat's REWORK 7195422188 asked for S1 and S2, plus N3 and N1 if cheap. The dev answered in report r2, comment 7196248359 on card #37556.

What I read:
- The delta, `git diff` from the old head to the new one. It touches two files: the hook (`useConsoleChatDock.tsx`, +35/-6) and its test.
- The net diff against `main`. It still has three files: the hook, the test, and the changeset. The changeset is unchanged since the old head.
- The check-runs on the new head: 55 in total, 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed. The required checks are all success: `Test UI` aggregate, `Type Check UI`, `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set.** No change. Nothing in the diff parses, validates or checks permissions. Right.
- **Public surface.** No change. Both new module-level names are private: `SHEET_WIDTH_BELOW` and `sheetShownAtInMemory`. `useConsoleChatDock` keeps the same signature and return shape. Right.
- **Behaviour change in the delta.** The hook now checks whether the user moved away from the history entry the sheet was shown on before it checks the phone flag. If so it sets `movedAwayRef`, and the collapse happens on the next run that knows the device is a phone. The phone check is the `isMobile` flag, which reads `false` on the first render. Three other changes:
  - The stored entry is dropped whenever the window is at desktop width, meaning `!isMobile` and `window.innerWidth` at least 768.
  - The module keeps an in-memory copy of the entry. It is written on every write and read only when sessionStorage throws.
- **Fence.** Held. The delta touches only the hook and its test.

Prior ids:

- **S1 — closed.** On a newly mounted host's first render, `isMobile` is still `false` but the width is under 768. In that render, a PUSH or POP to a different key now sets `movedAwayRef`. When the flag settles to phone on the next render, the ref is consumed and the sheet collapses, even if a REPLACE landed in between (for example `AppContent`'s alias redirect). I checked this against the real ordering. `AppContent` is the parent of `ConsoleLayout`, so the host's mount effect runs before the alias REPLACE effect, and it sees the PUSH. The new test pins this. Its `useIsMobile` stand-in has the real timing: `false` on first render, then measured in the mount effect. The `settleLate` variant goes further and makes the REPLACE land before the flag is measured. The dev reports this case is red against the old head's hook.
- **S2 — closed.** The new case "Back (a POP) away from the page the sheet was shown on closes it" mounts `[HOME, CITED]`, opens the sheet, and calls `navigate(-1)`. It expects the sheet closed. It goes red if the collapse is disabled (the dev's ablation: 6 red, 3 green).
- **N1 — closed.** At desktop width (`!isMobile` and `innerWidth` at least 768) the effect now clears both `movedAwayRef` and the stored entry. When the tablet turns back to portrait, there is no stored entry, so the sheet stays open and is stamped with the current key. Width is read off `window` rather than the `isMobile` flag. If the flag were used, a phone host's first-render `false` would wipe the entry on every remount, and S1 would come back. The case "turning a tablet to landscape and back does not close the drawer on the turn" pins this, and the dev reports it red against the old hook.
- **N2 — stays open, accepted.** The `"default"` key that every first entry of a document load shares is unchanged. The seat accepted it as is in REWORK 7195422188. It is harmless: the sheet stays open as it did before this PR.
- **N3 — closed.** The jsdoc now says the entry is kept in the module when sessionStorage throws. That copy covers every in-app navigation, layout swaps included. This is true: `writeSheetShownAt` sets the module copy before its try block, and `readSheetShownAt` returns it from its catch. The case "with sessionStorage throwing, a chip click still closes the sheet" pins it by making the `window.sessionStorage` getter throw.
- **N4 — closed.** Report r2 now says "Test UI aggregate and its affected legs". The wrong 16/16 count is gone.

New findings:

- **N5 (nit)** — `SHEET_WIDTH_BELOW = 768` repeats `MOBILE_BREAKPOINT` from `@object-ui/components`' `use-mobile.tsx`, which is not exported. The jsdoc names where it comes from, but if that breakpoint ever moves the two would drift apart. Between the two values, a phone host could then take the desktop branch, or the reverse. Exporting the constant from components and importing it here would remove the copy. Not blocking.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset.** `.changeset/37556-phone-dock-closes-on-citation.md` is unchanged in the delta and declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The delta adds no export, type or prop, only internal behaviour. Patch is still right. `Check Changeset` is success on the new head.
- **Clause-②: no.** Still right. No published spec, schema, metadata key or governed path is touched.
- **Metadata-protocol: none.** Still right. The only persisted state is the per-tab sessionStorage key, plus an in-memory copy that lasts for the page.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags.** Report r2 has `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, and `out_of_scope_findings: none`. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- **Booted alias check.** Report r2 describes a booted phone check of the alias path. It uses an injected citations part and a one-agent catalog, both disclosed. The chip went to `/apps/showcase_app/...`, which was REPLACEd to the package address, and the sheet closed. The screenshots are in the project files. The seat's landing terms ask for that screenshot on the delta. I am read-only here, so this is noted, not verified.
- **SQL push-down.** Not applicable. The diff does no data read, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

Coordinator's checks:

- **Can "recorded before the flag settles" collapse on desktop?** No. The only `collapse()` call sits after `if (!isMobile) return`. On a real desktop, every run takes the desktop branch first, because `!isMobile` holds and the width is 768 or more. That branch clears the ref and the entry and returns. The ref can only be set on a run where `innerWidth` under 768. If such a run happens with `isMobile` false, it returns before collapsing. On a later run where the flag says desktop, the ref is cleared, never consumed. The desktop-control case pins this, and so does the landscape leg of the tablet case.
- **Can it collapse on a REPLACE once the flag has settled on a phone?** No. Once `isMobile` is `true`, every run that sets the ref also consumes it in the same run (collapse) or clears it (sheet closed). So no set ref outlives a run. A REPLACE run never sets the ref, because the setting condition excludes `NavigationType.Replace`, so it stamps the new key. The ref can only carry across the one render before the flag settles. That carry is intended: it holds a PUSH or POP that has already happened. The REPLACE case pins the settled-phone direction.
- **Can the in-memory fallback keep a stale key across a real reload?** No. A reload re-evaluates the module, so `sheetShownAtInMemory` starts as `null`. When storage works the copy is written but never read. When storage throws, the drawer's own open state cannot persist across the reload either. A bfcache restore brings back the module heap together with the history entry it belongs to, so the copy and the location still agree.
- **Residual, ungraded.** A host that renders for the first time only after a REPLACE has landed would still treat that landing as a REPLACE. An example is a layout behind a Suspense boundary that resolves after the alias redirect. I found no such path on the record route: `AppContent` renders `ConsoleLayout` directly, and the alias REPLACE is `AppContent`'s own effect. I am not grading it.

No must-fix. No should-fix remains open.
